analysis.title: GS Molavi - Ruminations Macro, Micro, Markets 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: Market has lost momentum and confidence over the last 2-3 months. Violent risk-on/risk-off swings at stock, sector, factor and theme level keep P&L volatility high and make running gross and net exposure hard. Anchor themes are AI, oil and yields, supported by megacap strength, narrow leadership, earnings and belief in the future.

French OAT spread over bunds hit 140bps, a level not seen since 1990, on left vs right political dynamics and budget doubts, raising contagion concerns. UK budget and Spanish snap elections are also approaching, and Italy now looks comparatively stable.

Issuance fatigue is appearing: poor aftermarket performance for secondary supply globally and pulled primary deals (Firmus, following Bamboo and Oura). Broadcom and SpaceX have signalled capital raises for AI capex. Buyers are more discerning than in H1 on high rates and terminal value/ROI debate, though private markets still back pre-product AI companies.

Oil: the push-pull of escalation and de-escalation continued last week, with Riyadh airport attacks over the weekend as a low point. Mitigants (G7 reserves release, Trump/Putin diesel deal, re-routing, stockpile selling) are running dry. Molavi does not see spot oil normalising quickly: reserves would be rebuilt on any dip, shipping/insurance/logistics carry premiums, and refining of the product is structurally impaired. Oil can go lower only if many things go right, and the reasons for higher are growing.

P/E may be the wrong metric for the S&P. Molavi cites March 2000 (forward P/E 25.2, trailing operating P/E 39.3, GAAP about 60x) and 2007 (forward 15.1, 31.6x on EPS, over 100x GAAP). EPS at market tops is often wrong because of extrapolated peak margins, over-optimistic growth, late analyst cuts, flattering operating EPS and decaying earnings quality. Errors cost more when valuations and revenue run rates grow this fast.
Cyber names have strongly outperformed the S&P year to date: Okta +155%, Fortinet +138%, CrowdStrike +124%, Palo Alto +116%, Hack Cyber ETF +56%.

Concentration: the top 5 S&P companies have a combined market cap near $22T, about 30% of the index, equal in weight to 434 constituents. The 2013-14 average was about 200 stocks and the 2000 peak about 350.

Liquidity: average daily top-of-book liquidity fell 21% since 2023 (from $14m to about $11m). Top-of-book depth per $1B traded is $11k, down 93% from $162k in 2017. Daily volume tripled from 6.5bn to nearly 19bn shares since 2017. In June top-of-book depth fell 33% on a 2026 high of 22.8bn shares traded.
Scarcity pricing: 10-year-old supertankers trade at a premium to new ships. GPU pricing is up 17-21% across H100, H200, B200 and B300 generations.

Retail: internet searches for stocks to buy and for options trading are at the lowest weekly rate since August 2025, in a month retail normally re-engages. Robinhood data shows steady activity with rising leverage and margin use.

Credit: the market prices little credit risk (single-name default risk 1.3% at start of year vs 10.3% in 2007), but yields on AI capex financings are rising, IG and HY are moving higher and the CCC rally drew attention. CDS market shrank from about $61T in 2007 to about $11T while central bank balance sheets grew from $9T to $33.9T.

Jet fuel trades at roughly 1100-1400 vs a longer-term average of $700, a key input cost for airlines and the experience economy. Molavi doubts costs can be passed on to a K-shaped consumer facing higher food, fuel and financing costs, a weak savings ratio and a no-hire/no-fire labour market.

EM has beaten MSCI World in 6 of the last 9 market crashes (exceptions: 2022 inflation/Fed and 2018 Fed/trade war). Leadership has moved from India/Middle East to Korea/Taiwan to Brazil. A weaker dollar and developed-market fiscal pressure support further EM focus.

Ramp data shows company API token usage rising from 100 in Jan to 300 in June to over 700 in Sept, while token spend flattened from August and fell 5% last month despite peak token use. Molavi argues margin compression and mix shift between open-weight and frontier models are still net positive for AI infrastructure demand.

AI winners are up about 58-60% YTD vs S&P +13%, Nasdaq +22% and the median S&P stock -15%. The 'AI 10' are about 40% of S&P market cap. The AI orbit (megacaps, hyperscalers, neoclouds, labs, chips) is worth roughly $25-30T across public and private markets.

Twin peaks: historically capex peaked after the equity peak by 2 years (UK railways), 1 year (US utilities), 18 months (Japan), 7 months (dotcom) and 5 months (US shale), each time signalled by central bank policy shifts and rate rises. Equity prices are stalling and central banks have shifted and hiked, so capex is the item to watch.

Scale is consolidating across asset management (PE, multi-asset hedge funds, systematic quant, index/ETF). a16z raised close to 20% of 2025 venture capital, OpenAI raised $122bn at an $865bn valuation, and allocators are moving to larger cheques in fewer funds.
AI debt: Oracle 5-year CDS is near a record 261bps (pricing about a 20% default rate), SpaceX CDS implies 16% and Nvidia 7%. Over $500bn of debt has been issued this year to fund AI capex.

earnings_insights: No company earnings results are reported. The note says operating EPS flatters at market tops and that analysts are late to cut, so forward P/E understates risk.
Samsung and TSMC sales numbers were described as 'monster' but had little market impact, versus the immediate share-price impact of Meta's Muse on the consumer inertia theme.

risk_factors: French and European fiscal and political risk spreading to other bond markets.
Fatigue in equity and debt issuance as AI capex financing needs grow.
Oil supply mitigants running dry with the conflict continuing.
P/E understating risk if peak margins and optimistic growth are extrapolated.
Extreme index concentration in a handful of AI-linked megacaps.
Thin top-of-book liquidity makes large trades harder to execute.
Rising yields on AI capex financings and a possible capex peak following the stalling of equity prices.
Consumer strain from fuel, food and financing costs, with airlines exposed.
vol_and_positioning: Violent swings between risk-on and risk-off at stock, sub-sector, sector, factor and theme level, with rotation between momentum and value, size and broadening, and semis and software.
Top-of-book depth is thin despite tripled volumes, so signal and signal protection matter more. June depth fell 33% on 22.8bn shares traded.
Retail searches for stocks to buy and options trading are at the lowest weekly rate since August 2025, while Robinhood shows rising leverage and margin.
Top 5 S&P names are about 30% of the index and the AI 10 about 40%.
Ramp token data: token spend fell 5% last month despite peak token usage.
geopolitical: Escalation and de-escalation news flow around the Middle East oil conflict, including Riyadh airport attacks over the weekend.
G7 reserves release and a Trump/Putin diesel deal were attempted to ease supply.
Strait disruption affecting oil product flows, shipping and insurance costs.
French left vs right political dynamics and budget uncertainty, with the UK budget and Spanish snap elections approaching.

tension_points.bull_case: Token usage rose from 100 to over 700 and GPU prices are up 17-21%, so cheaper access should broaden demand for AI infrastructure and delivery layers.
tension_points.bear_case: Token spend flattened from August and fell 5% last month. Equity prices are stalling, central banks have shifted and hiked, and history shows capex peaking 5 months to 2 years after the equity peak.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A visible peak in AI capex after the equity stall and central bank rate rises, as in past cycles.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil can go lower if many things go right, including product flowing out of the strait and affordable shipping and insurance.
tension_points.bear_case: Reserves, re-routing and stockpile selling are running dry, reserves would be rebuilt on dips, logistics carry premiums and refining is impaired, so reasons for higher prices are growing.
